extracted.intended_audience: new or inexperienced workshop participants at the Bread Loaf Writers' Conference
extracted.subtask_short: workshopping creative writing at Bread Loaf
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for newcomers on how to prepare for, participate in, give, and receive feedback in Bread Loaf workshop sessions, including expectations of faculty, fellows, and peers. Emphasizes preparation, respectful critique practices, confidentiality, and post-workshop revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty and Fellows roles and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty members are chosen because they have vast experience teaching writers at all levels and are expected to help participants grow; Faculty offer feedback during workshop and schedule 30-minute individual meetings with each participant. Fellows are published authors assigned to workshops and assist as directed by the Faculty; their role can vary and some may offer individual meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty bring their own experience, style, and methodology; Faculty and Fellows are expected to lead workshops that are respectful of all participants. Faculty will schedule the 30-minute individual meeting with each participant. Fellow involvement beyond workshop depends on the Faculty's direction and is optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation (read Workshop Packet and assignments)
rubrics_metrics.description: On July 16 participants receive access to the Workshop Folder containing student manuscripts and an assignment to prepare for the first workshop; the assignment (and any outside reading) should be read and prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please commit to reading the Workshop Packet and preparing the first assignment; preparation is considered part of your agreement to maintain a respectful workshop space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect openness to feedback on your submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if your submission is wonderful, expect to receive feedback; you are at Bread Loaf to improve both your submitted piece and your craft, so be open to receiving constructive criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take notes but be discerning about what to incorporate. Remember that not all critiques are created equal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always read peers' submissions before workshop
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must read their peers' submissions before the workshop meets, and read them more than once if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take notes on reactions and thoughts while reading and be prepared to provide respectful, concrete comments. Expect to be asked to submit your comments; write clearly on the submitted piece or type your thoughts on a separate document. Reading peers increases your grasp of craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of workshop submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshop submissions should be treated with discretion and should never be shared or discussed with those outside of workshop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect the privacy of submissions to maintain trust and the integrity of the workshop environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure for offering critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of Faculty-specific guidelines, begin critiques with an objective description of the submission, then offer positive feedback and encouragement, followed by what you thought was not working.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective description helps establish trust and gives the writer the feeling their work has been seen. It's okay to note problems or lack of clarity even without a fix. Ask yourself if your comment will be useful. Avoid unhelpful statements like 'I don't like this' — prefer specifics like 'the character made me feel angry.' Your job is to help improve what's on the page within your allotted time, not to decide if the work is worthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific and useful rather than merely opinionated
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide concrete comments that help the writer understand reader response rather than just stating likes or dislikes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare 'I don't like this' (unhelpful) with 'the character made me feel angry' (specific and informative). Do not debate differing interpretations — readers absorb text in various ways and that variety is valuable to the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling sensitive subjects with respect
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussions about writing may involve race, gender, violence, trauma, and other potentially challenging subjects; participants must respect all workshop members and the lives reflected in submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect regards gender, gender identity and expression (including pronouns), age, sexual orientation, disability, body size, race, ethnicity, religion (or lack thereof). If something is troubling, communicate with your Faculty member or someone on staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving critiques: etiquette and behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Receive comments on your work respectfully; vulnerability while receiving feedback is normal and participants may respond in different ways (writing notes, avoiding eye contact, nodding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not interrupt while someone is giving feedback. After the reviewer has finished, you may ask questions for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not interrupt or argue during critique
rubrics_metrics.description: While receiving comments, interruptions are not appropriate; do not debate your understanding of the text during the feedback moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wait until the reviewer has finished to ask clarifying questions. Recognize that no two readers interpret text the same and there is no reason to debate interpretations in workshop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and timing of revision after workshop
rubrics_metrics.description: During revision, use the comments that resonate and set aside other comments for later review if you feel they may be useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If possible, begin revising your work within a month of your last workshop meeting, as the comments and ideas will be easier to recall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative follow-through (surveys)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the conference survey at the end of the conference to report on your workshop experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The conference solicits feedback about your workshop experience; participants are asked to complete this survey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect workshop as a learning community
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants are all strong writers from varied backgrounds; the workshop is a learning experience for everyone, including those new to workshop practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach workshop with humility and an openness to growth; thoughtful responding to others and listening to responses will increase your grasp of craft.
